question: Should OpenClaw adopt RFC 0018's opt-in canonical readiness contract, including subject identity and activation-scoped plugin providers, as the supported public direction?
rationale: The RFC introduces new configuration, endpoint-output, and plugin API commitments. The supplied discussion shows the proposal but no maintainer decision establishing which of those commitments OpenClaw intends to support.

options.title: Sponsor the RFC direction
options.body: Accept the opt-in readiness and provider model in principle, then record the agreed upgrade and compatibility boundaries in the RFC.

options.title: Narrow the first contract
options.body: Accept structured core readiness but defer plugin providers or subject identity to a later RFC.

options.title: Defer acceptance
options.body: Keep the RFC as draft until Gateway and plugin owners choose a smaller or different public readiness contract.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the RFC direction
recommendation.body: Accept the opt-in readiness and provider model in principle, then record the agreed upgrade and compatibility boundaries in the RFC.

likelyOwner.reason: They are best positioned to revise the RFC and linked implementation references after maintainers choose the direction.
